item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Katy made a table to keep track of how long it took water in a beaker to cool from 95°C to 70°C. She measured the time it took the water to cool in 5°C intervals.

| Interval Readings | Amount of Cooling Time |
| :--- | :--- |
| 95°C – 90°C | 2 minutes 10 seconds |
| 90°C – 85°C | 3 minutes 19 seconds |
| 85°C – 80°C | 4 minutes 48 seconds |
| 80°C – 75°C | 6 minutes 55 seconds |
| 75°C – 70°C | 9 minutes 43 seconds |

Estimate to the nearest minute the total time taken for the temperature of the water in the beaker to cool from 95°C to 70°C, and explain how your estimate was made.

Estimate: ____

Explain:

descriptors: 27 minutes, each amount of time is correctly rounded to whole minutes before adding (e.g., 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 10)
27 minutes, each amount of time is correctly rounded to the nearest 5, 10, 15, or 30 seconds
27 minutes, add minutes to equal 24 and uses some approach to estimate seconds to 3 minutes
27 minutes, adds correctly and then rounds off from 26 minutes 55 seconds
27 minutes. No calculations shown. Statements might include "rounded off to the nearest minute", "rounded the numbers up and down" or similar expressions
Method includes each amount of time correctly rounded to whole minutes before adding but answer is incorrect
Method includes each amount of time correctly rounded to the nearest 5, 10, 15, or 30 seconds but answer is incorrect
Other partially correct including 27 minutes with no explanation or method shown.
Each amount of time is rounded off, but one or more rounding is incorrect
25 minutes 75 seconds, 25.75 minutes; or rounds off from 25.75 minutes (or equivalent)
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.scoring_notes: Note: There is no distinction made between responses with or without units.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics)". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it.
